title: Pullback on global sections in dimension zero
statement: Let k and k′ be algebraically closed fields, f:C → Spec k a separated finite-type scheme of topological dimension at most zero [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], and let C′ → C, C′ → Spec k′, Spec k′ → Spec k be any cartesian square [def-pc-base-change]. For every abelian etale sheaf F on C [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the canonical global-sections pullback Γ(C,F) → Γ(C′,ι′⁻¹F), given by globalSectionsUpperStarMap [def-weil-pbc-finite-section-pullback], is bijective. Neither torsion nor reducedness is needed.

source.place: Proof steps 1 and 4 of the expanded DAG proof: the point bijection and compatibility of stalk germs. Stacks Tags 03Q1 and 0GJA.

proof.text: Obtain curve structure, dimension zero on C′, an equivalence b of point sets, and k′-valued geometric points t over all points of C′ from zeroDimensional_baseChange_geometric_points. Compose with ι′ and reindex by b.symm to obtain points s over C.

Apply zeroDimensional_sections_stalks twice to show the two products of identity-neighbourhood germ maps are isomorphisms. Compose with the explicit global-sections evaluation isomorphisms at the identity étale objects.

For each c′ obtain an inverse-image stalk isomorphism with the global-section germ equality from exists_globalSections_stalk_comparison. Combine these with Pi.mapIso and Pi.reindex. Verify the product equality by Pi.hom_ext, Pi.lift_π and the reindex projection formula. Cancel the isomorphisms on the right to prove the canonical global-sections map is an isomorphism, then apply ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective.

proof_origin.place: Second reading: genuine reduction via point choice, two existing stalk-product isomorphisms, single-stalk compatibility, Pi.mapIso and Pi.reindex.
